candidate.title: CaptureSeq
candidate.scope: The CaptureSeq (RNA capture sequencing) row of the assigned Illumina RNA Transcription schematic: two probe-design alternatives and one purified-RNA to indexed-cDNA, PCR and probe-capture route, ending at a target-enriched library. TruSeq stranded mRNA sample preparation is an embedded component, not a second target method. The lower RASL-seq row, overarching RNA Transcription heading, left-hand method icon and right-hand chemical legend are surrounding context, not connected CaptureSeq operations. The matching collection page is secondary catalogue evidence. The older primary paper clarifies the cDNA carrier and shared capture principle without making its preparation identical to this depicted implementation.

features: Final product drawn after capture-probe hybridization and its outgoing arrow.
Paper-supported interpretation: enriched RNA-derived cDNA library fragments are the sequencing carrier, despite the diagram’s RNA wording.
Enrichment shifts library representation toward chosen genomic/transcript regions; survival of capture does not prove perfect target specificity.

Sequence content can support discovery of exons and splice isoforms in targeted regions; abundance comparisons are supported in tested CaptureSeq applications, without implying unbiased whole-transcriptome sampling or unique-molecule counts.

operations.information_effect: Determines which RNA-derived sequences can be enriched and the discovery bias associated with that choice. The reference drawing guides target selection and is not mixed into the RNA sample.

operations.description: Convert purified RNA into a cDNA sequencing library carrying the depicted P5/P7 adapters and Index 2/Index 1 labels. operations.mechanism: RNA-to-cDNA library construction within the named TruSeq stranded mRNA block. Poly(A) selection, fragmentation and cDNA generation are clarification from the matching catalogue page, not separately drawn operations.

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Amplify the adapter-bearing cDNA library before the depicted hybridization stage, producing more copies of library fragments for capture.
operations.mechanism: Polymerase chain reaction of the cDNA library; no cycle count or other execution parameters are depicted.
operations.information_effect: Retains RNA-derived insert identity on amplified DNA molecules. The schematic supplies no unique-molecule identifier, so amplified copies are not independent biological molecule counts.

operations.label: Hybridize capture probes
operations.description: Expose the amplified cDNA library to capture probes specified by the target design; hybridization and the outgoing enrichment transition yield the final target-enriched library. The figure compresses capture/recovery into this transition and does not resolve its internal handling.
operations.mechanism: Complementary probe–cDNA hybridization selects RNA-derived library sequences. Physical probes are recognition reagents, while d_probe_design is a design constraint, not a molecule consumed in the reaction. The primary paper confirms that cDNAs, not native RNAs, are hybridized and sequenced.
operations.information_effect: Increases the fraction of sequencing library molecules associated with selected regions. Inserts carry biological sequence information, while probes determine what is enriched; target and off-target fragments need not be perfectly separated. Novel-exon discovery depends on the selected design and available captured fragments.
